# Deep Learning for Computer Vision

A practical course on deep-learning methods for visual understanding. Topics include neural-network foundations and practical training with PyTorch; convolutional architectures and model visualization; sequence models and vision transformers; generative models; self-supervised learning; implicit representations and neural rendering; and applications such as detection, segmentation, and image–text modeling.

## Course materials workflow

For this course, use the PDFs already stored in `materials/lectures/`. Do not assume lectures are in OneNote, ask to sync them, or use the shared OneNote lecture-sync workflow. The course's lecture materials are maintained directly as PDFs.

- Use `materials/lectures/deduped lectures/` as the default source for study and lecture questions.
- The deduplicated PDFs remove repeated cumulative slide-build pages. They are intended to retain all distinct lecture information while presenting it in fewer pages; they should contain the same substantive content as the originals, not a shortened summary.
- Use the matching PDF in `materials/lectures/original lectures/` to verify a visual detail or investigate anything that seems missing or ambiguous in a deduplicated copy.
- When PDF text extraction misses or garbles a figure, equation, or layout, inspect the relevant rendered PDF page rather than guessing.
